content: A urinary tract infection (UTI) is a bacterial infection that can affect any part of the urinary tract. Life-threatening causes are defined as conditions that may lead to death or permanent disability within 24 hours if left untreated. However, urinary tract infections do not have life-threatening causes. The most common causes of UTIs include the following pathogens: Escherichia coli Klebsiella pneumoniae Neisseria gonorrhoeae Proteus mirabilis Pseudomonas aeruginosa Staphylococcus saprophyticus Additionally, urinary catheterization is a common risk factor for developing a UTI. Management of UTIs involves an algorithmic approach that includes both diagnosis and treatment. This algorithm relies on symptoms and physical findings to guide clinical decisions. When treating UTIs, the following recommendations should be adhered to: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) should only be used during the second trimester of pregnancy. The following practices should be avoided: Do not use fluoroquinolones empirically for the treatment of acute uncomplicated cystitis. Avoid prescribing fluoroquinolones during pregnancy. Do not administer TMP-SMX during the first trimester or near term in pregnancy.
